### Why We Can Trust Jesus To Lead Us
Author: Lysa TerKeurst
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-august-29-2024.html
Passage: Ezekiel 34:23
Points:
- Human leaders and institutions can fail and break the trust of those they lead.
- God promised a dependable Shepherd who would genuinely nourish and care for His flock.
- Jesus fulfills Ezekiel's prophecy as the Good Shepherd who laid down His life for us.
- Christ knows each believer intimately, perceiving our needs far beyond mere head knowledge.
- Believers wounded by leaders can rebuild their confidence by following Jesus.

### Sheep and Goats
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/sheep-and-goats-one-year-devotions-for-men-april-22.html
Passage: Ezekiel 34:16-17
Points:
- People who suffer mistreatment desire justice, while abusers often seek cheap mercy.
- God inspects the hidden dealings between individuals and separates the gentle from the aggressive.
- The Lord promises to heal the injured while holding bullies accountable to His justice.
- Hoarding blessings while trampling what belongs to others invites God's righteous discipline.
- Experiencing God's mercy should compel believers to treat others fairly and justly.

### The Shepherd Rescues His Sheep
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/shepherd-rescues-his-sheep
Passage: Ezekiel 34:15-16
Points:
- Spiritual leaders bear serious accountability before God for how they shepherd His flock.
- Self-serving leaders who neglect the weak and appease sinners face divine removal.
- God intervenes personally to rescue His scattered sheep and administer true justice.
- The Lord binds up the wounded, strengthens the frail, and restores His flock to peace.
- Ezekiel's promise of the Davidic shepherd finds ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
